skill.name: extract-design-system
skill.description: Extract design primitives from a public website and generate starter design token files for a project.
skill.summary: Turns a public website URL into reviewed starter tokens for colors, fonts, spacing, radius, and shadows.
skill.author: arvindrk

security_audit.summary: The real risks are limited to intentional npx commands used to install Chromium and run the design-system extractor against public URLs. Most static hits are Markdown fences or output path references, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: External npx commands run package code and browser automation.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before running npx commands, and show the exact URL and command before execution.

remediation.issue: The target website and extracted JSON are untrusted third-party inputs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing review step and avoid applying generated tokens to app code without explicit user approval.

content.value_statement: Teams often need a quick starting point when matching a public website design. This skill extracts design primitives and guides review before generating starter token files.
actual_capabilities: Collects design primitives from a public website URL using extract-design-system.
Installs Chromium for Playwright when the local browser dependency is missing.
Generates raw extraction data and a normalized token representation.
Creates starter token files for colors, fonts, spacing, radius, and shadows when available.
Summarizes likely primary colors, font choices, and visual scales for review.
limitations: It does not create a complete component library.
It cannot guarantee pixel-perfect reproduction of a website.
It depends on public website reachability and visible page content.
It should not overwrite existing styling or configuration without confirmation.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a design token file
use_cases.description: Generate starter color, font, and spacing tokens from a public website before a redesign project.

use_cases.title: Audit visible brand primitives
use_cases.description: Review likely brand colors and typography from a public page before documenting a design baseline.

use_cases.title: Prepare migration inputs
use_cases.description: Create initial token artifacts that can be reviewed before applying styles to an existing application.

prompt_templates.title: Extract tokens from a site
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for the default workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract design primitives from this public website: <url>. Generate starter token files and summarize the results before changing any app code.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze without generating starter files
prompt_templates.prompt: Run extraction only for <url>. Review the normalized output and summarize colors, fonts, spacing, radius, and shadows.

prompt_templates.title: Regenerate tokens from existing extraction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the existing .extract-design-system/normalized.json file to regenerate starter token files. Do not fetch a website again.

prompt_templates.title: Review tokens for implementation readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before applying tokens to an app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the extracted design tokens, identify likely primary and secondary primitives, and recommend which tokens are safe to import into the app.

output_examples.input: Extract design primitives from a public marketing site.
output: A summary of likely primary, secondary, and accent colors.
Detected font families and available visual scales.
Generated starter token artifacts for review.

output_examples.input: Run extraction only for a site audit.
output_examples.output: The skill produces extraction artifacts and a concise review summary without creating starter token files.

output_examples.input: Regenerate token files from an existing normalized extraction.
output_examples.output: The skill rebuilds starter tokens from the saved normalized data and explains the generated files.

best_practices: Use a public and representative page for the first extraction.
Review normalized output before importing generated tokens into an app.
Ask for confirmation before modifying existing styles, config, or app files.
anti_patterns: Do not treat one page as proof of a complete product design system.
Do not infer semantic component tokens that were not clearly extracted.
Do not apply generated styles directly to production code without review.

faq.question: Does this build a full design system?
faq.answer: No. It creates starter token artifacts and a review summary, not a full component library.

faq.question: What inputs does it need?
faq.answer: It needs a public website URL and a choice between extraction only or starter file generation.

faq.question: What files can it generate?
faq.answer: It can generate raw extraction data, normalized token data, tokens.json, and tokens.css.

faq.question: Can it modify my app styles?
faq.answer: It should ask for explicit confirmation before changing existing app code, styles, or configuration.

faq.question: Does it work with dynamic sites?
faq.answer: It may work, but results can be incomplete when important content is hidden, dynamic, or behind authentication.

faq.question: Is extracted website content trusted?
faq.answer: No. The target website and generated extraction output should be reviewed as untrusted third-party input.
